name: phase 3 anomaly detection and failure prediction: evaluation set and pass marks
written_by: a one-task evaluation chat that is not the builder (A9)
phase_rules_read: Telemetry, when its schema entries are added
decided_by: Reece, question boxes on 4 November 2026; cost inputs 11 November 2026

decided_in_the_evaluation_chat.why: points where the approved plan and the tables disagreed, or where the plan gave no value
choices: At-risk rows follow the plan's rule (open-ticket days dropped, then no-running days); both counts are recorded, and the plan's split table shows the count before the no-running filter.
Warm-up: a pump-day is complete once the 90 days ending 8 days before it hold at least 60 readings. No train failure count is recorded, because the plan's 173 was not reproduced.
Seed 20230101, the data generator's seed; the five label shuffles use seed+1 to seed+5.
The recheck recomputes every headline metric: counts exactly, the rest within 1e-9 relative, as in phase 2. It reads the answer key for the warned flag, as evaluation only.
The control limit (E2) applies to the three models that read telemetry: the classifier, the robust z-score alone and the isolation forest alone.
Ties in the model grid go to max_leaf_nodes 15 before 31, then max_iter 100 before 200, then learning_rate 0.05 before 0.1.
Visit every pump: one visit per whole 30 days of the alert window, for every pump with a telemetry row in the window.
Fixed now: threshold candidates, 1,000 pump resamples, isolation forest at library defaults, ten reliability groups of equal row count.
Control run: features rebuilt and models trained again on the control telemetry with the same settings, then scored there.
Drift false flags are measured on July to December 2025, the months after the flag level's tuning data ends.

rests_on.plan: the approved phase 3 plan: sections Split dates, Labels and at-risk rows, Feature allowlist, Anomaly scores, Classifier, Alerts, catching a failure, and cost, Pass marks, Controls
rests_on.rule: A result counts only while these checksums hold. Code checks them before it runs and stops when one differs.

score.meaning: the model's estimate of the chance that this pump has a failure in the 30 days after this day, from readings up to the end of this day
score.ceiling: some failures give no warning, so no model can catch them; every result shows that share (W8)

periods.rule: E1: fixed by date before building. Labels look 30 days ahead, so each period's last labelled day is 30 days before its cut-off, and no training row's label window ends after its cut-off.

train.first_scored_day: each pump's first complete row, after its warm-up

periods.scored_days: pump-days scored for average precision; a period's step reads no row after its cut-off
periods.alert_window_days: alerts can open on any day of the alert window, the last 30 days included

no_complete_label_window.use: no part in training, thresholds or average precision; scored for the forward risk list risk_2025-12-31.csv, labelled 'no complete label window'

periods.no_refit: The model trained to 1 December 2024 is the one tested. Refitting on validation rows would need a new threshold (M3), with nothing left to choose it on.
periods.seasons: Validation is winter and spring, test is summer and autumn. A threshold that travels badly shows in the test result, and it is reported as it falls.
periods.test_scored: once per frozen configuration; eval/ml/split_lock.json holds the dates and the hash of the chosen settings, committed before the first test run, and the test step refuses to run without it (E1)
periods.dates_read_from: this file; code never types a date, and tests stop at the end of validation and take the test end from this file

expected_counts.source: counted from data/tables on 12 November 2026 at the commit above, from fact_service_event and fact_asset_telemetry, never the answer key; each pipeline step asserts its own counts against these (D15)

failures.period_of_a_failure: by reported_date: train to 2024-12-31, validation 2025-01-01 to 2025-06-30, test 2025-07-01 to 2025-12-31

failures_with_a_full_30_day_look_back.definition: failures reported on or after day 31 of the alert window (31 January 2025 for validation, 31 July 2025 for test), so the 30 days before them lie inside it
failures_with_a_full_30_day_look_back.train: not recorded: the plan's figure of 173 after a 90-day warm-up was not reproduced from the tables (170 failures have 90 days of telemetry before them)

rows_per_period.note: train is counted from the first telemetry day, before the warm-up filter

after_open_ticket_filter.note: the plan's split table shows these

at_risk_rows.note: after the no-running filter too; these are the rows scored

positive_share_percent.note: rounded to two decimals; code works out the exact share

expected_counts.warned_failures: left to evaluation code, which reads the answer key; this chat never opened it

labels.label: for pump p on day t: 1 when a Failure event for p has reported_date in (t, t+30], that is after day t and on or before day t+30; otherwise 0
labels.answer_key: never read for labels, features or the threshold (D10)

at_risk_rows.grain: one row per pump per day in fact_asset_telemetry
dropped_in_this_order: pump-days with an open failure ticket: reported_date <= day <= completed_date of a Failure event for the pump
days with no running, so no reading: running_hours is 0, and vibration and bearing temperature are blank
days before the pump has its baseline warm-up
at_risk_rows.warm_up: a pump-day is complete once the 90 days ending 8 days before it (days t-97 to t-8) hold at least 60 readings
at_risk_rows.reading: a day on which the pump ran, so vibration and bearing temperature are recorded
at_risk_rows.counted_and_asserted: each drop is counted and asserted (D15)
at_risk_rows.ticket_filter: It chooses rows and never feeds a feature. A ticket is open and known on the day, so it passes D11.

alerts.scores: one score per at-risk row; a dropped row has no score and opens no alert
alerts.alert: One alert is one visit. An alert opens when the score reaches the threshold (score >= threshold) on a pump with no open alert. The pump then stays quiet for 30 days, so a daily alert can't be counted as many visits.
alerts.caught: an alert opened 7 to 30 days before the failure: reported_date minus the alert day is from 7 to 30. Phase 4 plans by the week, so a day's notice doesn't help. One alert catches at most one failure.
alerts.wasted: an alert with no failure in the next 30 days. An alert in the last 30 days of a period with no failure yet counts as wasted, the cautious reading.
alerts.neither: an alert opened 1 to 6 days before a failure is neither caught nor wasted: the failure is missed and the visit adds no cost. This follows from the two definitions above.
alerts.missed: a failure reported in the alert window that no alert caught
alerts.unwarned_failures: They can't be prevented under any plan: they always cost a miss, and an alert that happens to precede one counts as wasted. They are reported apart.
alerts.warned_failure: a failure the answer key in data/generator-truth/ marks as having a warning; only evaluation code and the recheck read it (D10)
alerts.failures_counted: Failure events with reported_date in the alert window

cost.formula: cost = missed failures x cost of a missed failure + wasted visits x cost of a wasted visit
cost.useful_visit: The missed-failure input is the extra cost over a repair planned in advance, so a useful visit adds nothing.

plans.window: all three plans are compared over the same alert window
plans.visit_none: no visits; every failure is missed

visit_every_pump.rule: one visit per pump every 30 days
visit_every_pump.visits: for every pump with a telemetry row in the alert window, one visit per whole 30 days of the window: 6 per pump in each window (181 and 184 days)
visit_every_pump.caught: it is given every warned failure, which is generous to it
visit_every_pump.wasted_visits: its visits minus the warned failures it is given

inputs.read_in_code: code reads each value from the source file when it runs; no cost value is typed in this file or in code

central.use: the threshold and the pass mark

inputs.covers: the missed-failure cost covers Fjordvik's repair cost only; the customer's downtime cost and expedited parts are left out, as the source file says
inputs.basis: worked out from Fjordvik's synthetic tables times published rates; not real-world costs

cost.sensitivity_table: the three plans' costs at the low, central and high missed-failure cost, with the alerts unchanged (the threshold chosen at the central cost); reported beside the result, never a pass mark

threshold.rule: M3: chosen on validation only, from the costs, using failures from fact_service_event and no answer key, so it can run on live data
threshold.criterion: lowest cost of the model plan over the validation alert window at the central missed-failure cost, counting every failure as preventable
threshold.candidates: every distinct score on the validation at-risk rows in the alert window
threshold.ties: ties go to fewer visits; if still tied, the higher threshold
threshold.stored: with the model version, in eval/ml/split_lock.json and the model card; the test step refuses a threshold from another version; chosen again after every retrain

metrics.average_precision: the sum over score thresholds of (recall at n minus recall at n-1) times precision at n, as scikit-learn's average_precision_score defines it, on a period's at-risk rows in its scored days
metrics.dummy: DummyClassifier(strategy="prior"); its average precision equals the positive share of the rows scored
metrics.recall_of_warned_failures: warned failures caught divided by warned failures reported in the alert window, at the chosen threshold
metrics.cost: the formula above for each of the three plans, at the central missed-failure cost
metrics.headline: M4: average precision, recall of warned failures, and cost against the visit-every and visit-none plans. Accuracy and the area under the ROC (receiver operating characteristic) curve are never shown alone. The report states the share of positive rows.
metrics.range: a 90% range for each headline metric: 1,000 resamples of pumps with replacement, seeded, 5th to 95th percentile
metrics.reliability_table: score group against observed failure rate, on validation and on test: ten groups of equal row count by score
metrics.one_failure: the plan estimates about 34 warned failures in the test period, so one failure moves recall by about 0.03; the range shows it

pass_marks.set_by: Reece, the approved phase 3 plan; fixed, never changed to pass (A9)
pass_marks.scope: the test period, scored once; the chosen threshold; the central missed-failure cost
wording: Average precision at least 3 times the dummy's. The dummy's equals the positive share, so about 0.046 on test.
At the chosen threshold, recall of warned failures at least 0.6, and cost below both plans.
Unwarned failures reported apart, and the leakage test passing.
Set here before building: the shuffled-label control, E2 band and M5 limits.

average_precision.of: the classifier, on the test at-risk rows scored 1 July to 1 December 2025

recall_of_warned_failures.at: the chosen threshold, over the test alert window

cost.at: the chosen threshold and the central missed-failure cost, over the test alert window

pass_marks.controls: the shuffled-label, E2 and M5 limits below are met

time_and_group.time: the time split above; never shuffled rows
time_and_group.group: 5-fold GroupKFold by pump over train and validation rows, with the chosen settings, reported next to the validation score so the gap is visible; test rows take no part

checks: a rebuild with every row after day t deleted must not change the features at 20 random pump-days
a planted bad feature (a centred window) must fail the test, to prove it can
the model's feature list sits inside eval/ml/feature_allowlist.json
a recorder around file opens proves the feature path opens only its four tables
an import check proves only evaluate.py names generator-truth

shuffled_labels.method: the training labels are shuffled, the classifier is trained again with the chosen settings and scored on validation
shuffled_labels.statistic: mean average precision over the 5 shuffles
shuffled_labels.why_a_band: a tolerance for sampling noise, fixed now

control_telemetry.data: control/fact_asset_telemetry.csv, built by python -m fjordvik_data.scenarios into service-ai/build/ml-scenarios/ and checked against data/scenarios/manifest.json; the warning rise is switched off for every failure, with the same seed
models: the robust z-score alone (z_max as the score)
the isolation forest alone (iforest_score as the score)
control_telemetry.method: features are rebuilt and each model is trained again on the control telemetry with the same settings, then scored there; no setting or threshold is chosen again
control_telemetry.of: each model's average precision against the dummy's on the same rows
control_telemetry.run_on: validation before the lock, and test in the single test run
control_telemetry.reported_beside: the dummy and the pump-facts-only model, which explains the control result because age and pump type move the failure rate even with warnings off

drift.monitor: per pump and sensor, the 7-day median against the same pump's median for the same calendar month in earlier years; never the last few weeks

scenarios.source: drift_recalibration/ and drift_unit_change/ fact_asset_telemetry.csv and drift_scenarios.csv, built by the scenarios module and checked against data/scenarios/manifest.json
scenarios.drift_recalibration: a recalibration step in bearing temperature
scenarios.changed_pumps: the rows of drift_scenarios.csv: asset_id, scenario, start_date, sensor, change

detection.of: the changed pumps in each scenario, each judged apart: a pump counts when the monitor flags its changed sensor on a day from start_date to start_date plus 14

false_flags.of: pump-months flagged on the base data with no failure in the following 42 days, as a share of the monitored pump-months
false_flags.late_flags: a flag with fewer than 42 days of data after it counts as a false flag when no failure follows by 31 December 2025, the cautious reading

drift.flag_level: chosen on base data up to the end of validation (30 June 2025); never on the scenarios or on later months
drift.not_monitored: pumps with no earlier year for the month are reported as not monitored

model.classifier: scikit-learn HistGradientBoostingClassifier, no class weights; the threshold handles the imbalance, so the output stays a usable probability
model.outside_the_grid: a setting that is not in the grid is not tuned: it stays at the library's default and is recorded in the model card

chosen_on_validation.criterion: highest average precision on the validation at-risk rows scored 1 January to 1 June 2025; ties go to the simpler
chosen_on_validation.recorded_in: eval/ml/split_lock.json, committed before the first test run

baselines.pump_facts_only: report only: the classifier on age_years, product_group, application, rated_kw and service_contract; it shows what the telemetry adds

anomaly_scores.robust_z_score: (7-day median minus baseline median) divided by (1.4826 times the baseline median absolute deviation), on fleet-adjusted readings
anomaly_scores.isolation_forest: fitted on training rows only, on the z-scores and changes; scikit-learn's default settings, the seed, n_jobs=1
anomaly_scores.judged: both through the classifier and alone, by average precision

seed.same_as: the data generator's seed in data/scenarios/manifest.json
seed.generator: numpy RandomState(PCG64(seed)), an explicit bit generator (G10)
seed.repeat: training twice on the same data gives the same metrics (G10)

recheck.script: scripts/recheck_ml.py: standard library only; imports nothing from the fjordvik_service package
recheck.reads: the saved score and alert files in results/ml/, the raw tables, data/scenarios/planning_inputs.json and, for the warned flag only, the answer key (evaluation only, D10)
recomputes: average precision of the dummy, and the ratio of the two
the number of alerts, and of alerts caught, wasted and neither
the number of failures missed, and of warned and unwarned failures
the cost of the visit-none, visit-every-pump and model plans at the central missed-failure cost

tolerance.others: relative 1e-9: |recomputed - saved| <= 1e-9 x max(1, |saved|), as in phase 2

recheck.fails: any metric outside its tolerance fails the recheck; its output is saved in evidence/

reporting.basis: W8: every result says it was measured on synthetic data with planted signals, and never presents it as performance on real pumps
reporting.stamps: G10: every saved result names the data checksum, the commit and the model version
